Iron ore in structural decline; BHP under existential pressure as China demand weakens amid US-China trade tensions
Home buyer sentiment collapses to new milestone; property sector facing 'GFC moment' with mortgage stress driving second-job uptake
Santos gas cartel breaking, reshaping energy sector dynamics; gold discoveries (Forrestania, Kaiser, Larvotto) support miners
S&P 500 short interest at decade highs; global risk-off tone with Wall Street drifting lower
Qantas $35M redundancy payout and in-flight incident weigh on QAN.AX; small business 'insidious cost creep' pressures consumer sector

sectors.trend: Iron ore in freefall ('drowning, not waving'); BHP facing existential strategic review. Gold counter-cyclical strength with multiple ASX-relevant discoveries (Forrestania 2Moz, Kaiser Tassie, Larvotto NSW). Uranium exploration active (Infini, Canada).
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX under severe pressure on weak China demand and US-China trade friction. Gold miners (GOLD.AX, NVL.AX, WES.AX) and uranium names offer relative strength. Diversify away from iron ore exposure.

sectors.trend: Big four banks falling as oil-driven inflation fears raise RBA rate-hike odds. Property sector stress (buyer sentiment collapse, GFC comparisons) threatens NPL trajectories. ATO intensifying Big Tech tax enforcement.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX face margin compression from rate volatility and property credit risk. REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX) vulnerable to sentiment deterioration. Monitor RBA commentary closely.

sectors.trend: Oil near US$100 on Hormuz Strait escalation and Middle East flare-up. Santos gas cartel breaking, potentially reshaping domestic gas pricing and LNG export economics.
sectors.implications: WDS.AX, WLE.AX, BRL.AX benefit from oil spike. Santos (STO.AX) faces strategic overhang as gas cartel dynamics shift. LNG exporters (BHP.AX, WDS.AX) gain on higher energy prices.

sectors.trend: Small businesses fighting 'insidious cost creep'; 102-year-old mall retailer closing 25 stores; Qantas $35M payout and safety incident; beverage brand Chapter 11. Living standards under pressure.
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WBC.AX (retail), QAN.AX under pressure. Consumer discretionary names vulnerable. Defensive staples (WOW.AX, WES.AX) preferred.

sectors.trend: Diagnostic delays causing mental distress; rural doctor drought; Tasmanian surgery wait targets 'lowering the bar'. Structural underfunding signals.
sectors.implications: CSL.AX, SGH.AX, HIC.AX benefit from long-term healthcare demand but face policy uncertainty. Rural health providers may attract government support.

sectors.trend: Nvidia strong results reinforce AI outlook; Palo Alto Networks strong FCF. S&P 500 short interest at decade highs. ATO vs Big Tech tax battle. Foreign AI deepfake network targeting Australian politicians.
sectors.implications: Global tech strength (NVDA, PANW) supports sentiment but S&P short interest signals fragility. ASX tech (WTC.AX, XRO.AX) limited but benefit from global AI capex cycle.

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely volatile and range-bound. Oil spike near US$100 and Hormuz risk support energy names but fuel rate-hike fears, pressuring banks and property. Iron ore weakness caps materials. Expect ^AXJO to trade in a tight range with sector rotation toward energy and gold. RBA commentary is the key swing factor.
market_outlook.long_term: Structural headwinds persist: iron ore demand plateau, property correction, living standards squeeze. Gold, uranium, and energy offer relative strength. Healthcare and infrastructure (tradies scheme, 6,000 qualifications) provide policy tailwinds. Global tech (Nvidia, PANW) remains a positive but S&P fragility limits spillover. 6-12 month view: cautious, favour quality and dividends.
